glossary.definition: A small set of essential, timeless pieces supplemented by seasonal items, designed so pieces cross-combine; the term was coined by Susie Faux, owner of the London boutique 'Wardrobe', in the 1970s [FACT — capsule-history sources in the grounding file].

Donna Karan's 1985 mainstreaming of the capsule idea: bodysuit, skirt, tailored jacket, dress, something leather, white shirt, cashmere sweater — interchangeable pieces taking a woman from office to evening [FACT — grounding file sources 25-26].

This program's unit of pre-built clothing: a named, fixed descriptor paragraph (garments, fabrics, colors, closures, accessories) reused verbatim in prompts, shipping with an optional garment Element, a formality band 1-5, and an allowed-scenes list [ESTIMATE — authored transfer of capsule theory to AI production].

The styling register of the program: understated elegance, 'an almost aggressive absence of branding' with no logo larger than a thumbnail, tailoring and fabric quality doing the signaling that logos would [FACT — Wikipedia 'Quiet luxury' + old-money guides, grounding sources 28-31].

The 1-5 scale every module and scene carries: 1 gym/beach, 2 resort-day, 3 smart-casual/travel, 4 dinner/cocktail, 5 gala/black-tie; pieces may cross-combine within plus/minus one band [ESTIMATE — authored combination grammar].

The authored restraint rule that an outfit carries at most one statement (a bold coat OR a bold accessory, never both), because quiet luxury reads through restraint [ESTIMATE — authored from quiet-luxury editorial logic].

The rule that linen/poplin modules appear only in sun scenes and tweed/cashmere-overcoat modules only in cool scenes, because a fabric-season mismatch is an instant AI tell [ESTIMATE — authored craft rule].

A Higgsfield reference Element (categories character|environment|prop, created instantly from one or a few images, no training) materializing a wardrobe module so the garment is reference-anchored, embedded as a <<<element_id>>> placeholder in the prompt; not usable with the Soul models [FACT — live MCP surface via higgsfield_surface.md].

The bible rule that hair is always described in five slots — length + texture + color + part side + finish — with no slot ever dropped and identical phrasing forever, because generators treat synonyms as different visual tokens [ESTIMATE — authored craft on top of the grounding file's consistency-guide consensus].

A named, enumerated grooming configuration per persona (e.g. male: 'clean-shaven' only or one fixed stubble grade; female: makeup 'polished-natural' default, 'evening glam' for gala only), matched against the scene card at QC; stubble length wobbles badly between generations, so a single grade is picked and policed [ESTIMATE — authored craft].

A module whose descriptor drifts across prompts is not a module; it is per-shot styling wearing a name.

nodes.definition: Define the formality scale every module and scene carries, because band arithmetic is what replaces case-by-case judgment in combination decisions. Bands [ESTIMATE — authored grammar, grounding §6]: 1 gym/beach · 2 resort-day · 3 smart-casual/travel · 4 dinner/cocktail · 5 gala/black-tie. Every module is assigned exactly one band at authoring time; every scene in the dress-code matrix is assigned a band (or a narrow range like the luxury-car night drive's 3-4). The band does two jobs: (a) it gates module-to-scene assignment (a band-1 module never appears in a band-5 scene), and (b) it powers the plus/minus-one cross-combination rule in the grammar (M2's band-2 trousers may join M8's band-3 blazer; M6's band-1 sneakers may never join M4's band-5 black tie). Bands are coarse on purpose — five levels is enough to catch every genre-breaking mismatch while leaving room for the owner's flexibility inside a band.

Checks: (1) wardrobe module rendered faithfully — fabric, color, CLOSURE details against the module descriptor (and against the garment Element image where one exists); (2) hair verified on all five slots, and the correct scene-bound variant present; (3) grooming state matches the scene card string (beard grade / makeup level / nail color); (4) fabric-season coherence (no linen in cool scenes, no tweed in sun); (5) zero logos, monograms or brand marks anywhere; (6) accessory continuity — watch, jewelry set, bag family, nail color consistent with the bible AND with adjacent clips in the stitched reel; (7) in duo frames, both personas' wardrobe verified independently, including band agreement between their modules; (8) band and palette legality of any combination, with off-matrix combos checked for a log entry. A batch fails the gate on any un-waived miss; waivers route through the flexibility clause and are logged. Whether garment-Element-anchored modules fail these checks less often than text-only modules is the run-phase experiment that resolves this KB's central [UNKNOWN].

conflict_axes.name: strict_matrix_vs_owner_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: The scene matrix and grammar want every outfit predictable and checkable, while the owner explicitly asked for flexible combination — modules as defaults, not law.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: flexibility wins at decision time (owner's clause), predictability is recovered by the logging protocol: fixed text even for one-offs, promotion to a named module on first reuse

conflict_axes.name: text_anchored_vs_element_anchored_garments
conflict_axes.description: A wardrobe module can live as a verbatim descriptor paragraph, as a garment Element reference, or both — Elements promise closure/fabric fidelity but are Soul-incompatible and their fidelity is UNKNOWN on this surface.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry both: text always rides and stays the QC ground truth; Elements are additive on compatible models until the run-phase A/B miss-rate experiment resolves the UNKNOWN

conflict_axes.name: statement_styling_vs_quiet_restraint
conflict_axes.description: Feed-level visual interest pushes toward bold pieces while the quiet-luxury register reads through restraint — the one-statement rule caps boldness per outfit.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: restraint wins by default (one statement maximum); owner-driven statement exceptions route through the flexibility clause and never stack two statements in one outfit

conflict_axes.name: brand_reference_vs_brand_depiction
conflict_axes.description: The genre is calibrated on named reference houses (Loro Piana, Brunello Cucinelli, Savile Row tailors), yet the no-logo philosophy and the honesty contract forbid claiming or depicting brand identity in generated content.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: houses inform the human author's fabric/fit vocabulary only; prompts carry fabric and construction words, never brand names, and any rendered logo or monogram is an automatic QC reject

conflict_axes.name: fabric_season_authenticity_vs_scene_variety
conflict_axes.description: Scene variety tempts reuse of a favorite module everywhere, but linen in a cool scene or tweed in Riviera sun is an instant AI tell that breaks the realism requirement.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the fabric-season lock never waives — it is one of the two rules the flexibility clause cannot override; variety comes from adding modules, not from season-breaking reuse

conflict_axes.name: duo_matching_vs_complementary
conflict_axes.description: Couple-content conventions include deliberate twinning, but matching outfits read costume/promotional against the two-individuals register this program stages.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: complementary wins by default (his navy, her ivory; never identical head-to-toe); deliberate matching is an owner-level format decision, not a per-shot option

conflict_axes.name: loose_hair_realism_vs_wind_continuity
conflict_axes.description: The female default (soft waves down) is the persona's signature look, but in yacht/wind scenes loose tidy hair is physically implausible and the generator fights to hold it, producing drift.
poles: keep the signature loose hair everywhere
switch to the pre-authorized wind variant
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the wind variant wins in wind-class scenes — it is both more physically honest and more continuity-safe; the signature look remains the default everywhere else

conflict_axes.name: fitness_appeal_vs_genre_consistency
conflict_axes.description: Fitness content pulls toward generator-typical athletic styling (neon, compression-shine, sports logos) that maximizes the fitness read but breaks the classic-luxurious genre.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: genre wins: heritage-athletic register only (tennis whites, rowing knits, monochrome logo-free sets), physique carried by fit not shine; the appeal question itself belongs to the psychology file

conflict_axes.name: per_shot_improvisation_vs_versioned_change
conflict_axes.description: Creative momentum favors adjusting hair, grooming and accessories per shot, while continuity across hundreds of generations demands that every change be either a pre-authorized variant or a versioned bible event.
poles: change only via variants and versions
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the two-channel rule wins: scene-bound variants for instant needs, bible versions for lasting changes; silent per-shot improvisation is outlawed because it is indistinguishable from drift at QC

priority_rationale: The foundations (capsule pattern, module format, persona palettes, formality bands) come first because every module, matrix row and grammar rule is expressed in their vocabulary; the published style codes (menswear, black tie, womenswear, fitness register) next because modules must be code-checked at authoring time, not retrofitted; the module libraries and scene matrix then turn codes into the pre-built, per-scene lookups the owner asked for; the grammar layer (combination rules, flexibility clause with logging, accessory set, duo coordination) governs flexible recombination without letting it decay into drift; the platform node constrains garment anchoring to what the live Higgsfield surface actually supports; the grooming stack (canons, five-slot lock, state enum, wind variants and versioning) locks the hair-and-grooming continuity that rides in every prompt; and the QC gate comes last because it is where every upstream rule becomes an enforced check and where the system's central UNKNOWN (Element vs text fidelity) gets its evidence.
